Run the Fully Simulation-Based Sample Size Pathway

Source: R/pmgen_simulate.R
pmgen_simulate.Rd

For each value in N, draws n_sims development datasets of size N from the joint predictor distribution, fits the chosen model on each, evaluates it on the fixed target population, and computes requested performance metrics. Results are summarised into a pmgen_result object.

Usage

pmgen_simulate(
  ref_model,
  target_pop,
  N,
  n_sims = 1000L,
  method = "logistic",
  method_args = list(),
  threshold = 0.5,
  metrics = c("cstat", "cal_slope", "mape", "net_benefit"),
  store_predictions = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

ref_model

A pmgen_ref_model object from pmgen_reference().

target_pop

A pmgen_target_pop object from pmgen_target_population().

N

Integer vector of development sample sizes to evaluate.

n_sims

Integer. Number of simulation draws per N value. Default 1000.

method

Character string naming a built-in method ("logistic", "ridge", "lasso", "elasticnet", "firth"), or a user-supplied function with signature (train_data, predictors, outcome_col, method_args) that returns a prediction closure. See Details.

method_args

Named list of method-specific tuning arguments passed through to the fit function. For "logistic": shrinkage = TRUE applies van Houwelingen uniform shrinkage; separation = "drop" (default) or "keep" sets how perfect prediction is handled (see Details). For "ridge", "lasso", "elasticnet": nfolds, type.measure, lambda. For "elasticnet": alpha (required). For "firth": maxit, maxstep.

threshold

Numeric in (0, 1). Clinical probability threshold used for net benefit and ERVSI calculations. Default 0.5.

metrics

Character vector of metrics to compute. Any of: "cstat", "cal_slope", "cal_intercept", "oe_ratio", "mape", "rmspe", "brier", "net_benefit", "ervsi". Default: c("cstat", "cal_slope", "mape", "net_benefit").

store_predictions

Logical. If TRUE, the full matrix of predicted probabilities on the target population is stored for every simulation draw (a n_pop x n_sims matrix per N value). Required for plot(result, type = "instability") and plot(result, type = "calibration"). Memory use: approximately n_pop * n_sims * 8 bytes per N value (~750 MB for n_pop = 100,000 and n_sims = 1,000). Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for reproducibility (see Reproducibility in Details). Default NULL, which uses the session's random number stream.

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages per N value. Default TRUE.

Value

A pmgen_result object. Use summary(), print(), and plot() methods to inspect results, and pmgen_min_n() to identify the minimum sample size meeting specified criteria. Element fit_info is a data frame giving, for each N, the number of failed fits (n_failed) and of fits in which predictors were dropped for perfect prediction (n_dropped); dropped_predictors is a matrix (one row per N) of how often each predictor was dropped.

Details

Parallel execution: If the furrr package is installed, the simulations are run with furrr::future_map(), so they follow whatever future plan is set. Set a parallel backend before calling pmgen_simulate() for speed:

future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)
result <- pmgen_simulate(...)
future::plan(future::sequential)  # reset afterwards

Without a parallel plan, or without furrr, execution is sequential.

Reproducibility: The simulations for each value of N use seeds that depend only on seed, that N value and n_sims. So, for a given seed:

  • results are identical whether run sequentially or in parallel, with any future plan and any number of workers;

  • results for an N value do not depend on the other values in N: N = 400 gives the same results in N = c(200, 400) as in N = c(400, 600), so a grid can be extended without re-running the values already done;

  • increasing n_sims keeps the earlier simulations: the first 500 simulations with n_sims = 1000 are the simulations with n_sims = 500.

Each simulation uses the session's random number generator settings (base::RNGkind()), including on parallel workers. Results for a given seed can differ between versions of R if the generators change. pmgen_simulate() changes the session's random number stream only by calling set.seed(seed) (if seed is given) and making one draw.

The "ridge", "lasso" and "elasticnet" methods need the glmnet package, and "firth" needs logistf.

Custom methods: Supply a function of the form

my_method <- function(train_data, predictors, outcome_col, method_args) {
  # fit some model on train_data
  function(new_data) {
    # return vector of predicted probabilities
  }
}
result <- pmgen_simulate(..., method = my_method)

Development data: At each simulation iteration, N rows are sampled with replacement from ref_model$joint_data. Binary outcomes are generated from the reference model's true risks (Y ~ Bernoulli(plogis(X %*% beta))). A warning is issued if N exceeds the number of rows in joint_data.

Perfect prediction (method = "logistic"): In small development samples, one level of a binary predictor can have the same outcome for everyone (e.g. all treated patients have the event). Maximum likelihood then gives that predictor an effectively infinite coefficient, which distorts the model's predictions. With method_args = list(separation = "drop") (the default), before each fit any two-valued predictor with a level whose outcome is constant is dropped, together with the observations at that level; this is repeated until no such predictor remains, and the remaining predictors are fitted. Dropped predictors get a coefficient of 0 when predicting. If a predictor with more than two values separates the outcome completely, the fit fails and that simulation's metrics are NA. Use separation = "keep" to fit stats::glm() to all predictors and observations as they are. The penalised methods ("ridge", "lasso", "elasticnet", "firth") handle separation themselves and ignore this argument.

Failed fits: If fitting or prediction fails in a simulation, its metrics are NA and are left out of the summaries. A warning gives the number of failed fits for each N and the first error message.

References

Riley RD, Whittle R, Sadatsafavi M, Martin GP, Pate A, Collins GS, Ensor J. A general sample size framework for developing or updating a predictive algorithm: with application to clinical prediction models. BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:121. doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02856-7

Examples

# Small settings so the example runs quickly. In practice use the
# pmgen_reference() defaults, n_sims = 1000 or more, and a finer N grid.
ref <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data = dvt_data, predictors = setdiff(names(dvt_data), "dvt"),
  prevalence = 0.21, cstatistic = 0.78,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e5, n_synth = 1e5, seed = 42
)
#> Running bisection to calibrate reference model...
#> Bisection converged: prevalence=0.2100 (target=0.2100), c-stat=0.7791 (target=0.7800)
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.
tp <- pmgen_target_population(ref, n = 5000, seed = 42)

result <- pmgen_simulate(ref, tp, N = c(250, 1000), n_sims = 20,
                         method = "logistic",
                         metrics = c("cstat", "cal_slope", "mape"),
                         seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)
result
#> pmgen result
#> ------------

#>   N values            : 250, 1000

#>   Predictions stored  : no
#>

#>   250 cal_slope 0.74127221 0.152276595 0.50331683 1.07611004     -0.271161746
#>   250      mape 0.06850693 0.014447641 0.04981431 0.09782688      0.068506927
#>  1000     cstat 0.78977302 0.003275223 0.78456655 0.79526384     -0.001456249

summary(result)
#>      N    metric       mean          sd       q025       q975 degradation_mean
